lines.text: A very long password could log attackers into some Alpine Linux servers.
Servers check a password by scrambling it into a hash and comparing it with the stored one.
lines.title: How passwords are checked

lines.text: Accounts with no password store just a star symbol in that field.
lines.title: No-password accounts

lines.text: But for passwords over 256 bytes, the scrambling function fails and returns that same star as its error.
lines.title: The bug

lines.text: Star equals star, so the server thinks the password is right and lets the attacker in.
It needs a no-password account, and at least one other account with a normal password.
lines.title: Who is at risk

lines.text: The fix: update openssh, then restart sshd. Updating alone does not replace the running server.
lines.title: How to fix it

lines.text: If you can't update yet, turn off password logins.
lines.title: Takeaways
